newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir slams Malaysian Airlines critics.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir slams Malaysian Airlines critics.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said criticism about service and morale at national carrier Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) was aimed at discrediting the airline and its chairman.
"If we want to bring down our own airline, then the criticisms should continue," the New Straits Times newspaper quoted him as saying. "Others, too, won't fly it."

Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sunday that the government had begun an inquiry into MAS after a local newspaper reported service was deteriorating, partly due to a lack of pilots and cabin crew.

MAS Chairman Tajudin Ramli, who was awarded control of the airline under a privatisation deal in 1994, said in a statement on Monday that some of the issues raised were not new. Management was aware of them and was just as concerned, he said.

In previous remarks, Tajudin said he had initiated a restructuring at the former government-run airline to trim its bloated work force and merge or spin off some departments, such as catering and engineering.
The New Straits Times quoted Mahathir as saying it looked like there was some sort of campaign to undermine Tajudin.

Asked about reports that Tajudin wanted to sell the airline, Mahathir said: "Those are just rumours...I asked Tajudin whether it was true and he said he had no intention of selling," the newspaper quoted Mahathir as saying.
"However, those interested in the airline may have started a campaign to give the impression that he could no longer manage MAS and should therefore sell it off," he said.

MAS, which is in the midst of a fleet expansion, including the purchase of 25 Boeing 737 and 747 aircraft, is recruiting additional pilots and has another 400 cabin crew staff undergoing training, Tajudin said in his statement last week.
Mahathir said part of the problem was that MAS had greatly expanded the number of routes it was flying after the government negotiated new landing rights to position the carrier as a global airline.
